chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Humran, who said:

The sacrificial camels became expensive in Mina one year, to the extent that the single camel reached one hundred dinars. So Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) was asked about that, and he (peace be upon him) said: 'Participate in it [share in it].' I said, 'How many?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Whatever is lighter, so it is superior.' I said, 'On behalf of how many would it suffice?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'On behalf of seventy.'

key_terms.دِينَارٍ: Dinar, a gold coin used as currency
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, a location near Mecca where Hajj rituals take place

ai.seo_question: How many people can share in one sacrificial camel according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) clarifies that while sharing a camel is permissible, the principle of 'ease' (khaff) dictates that the share should be minimal to maximize participation, setting the lower limit at seventy dirhams. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on facilitating religious obligations during times of economic hardship, distinguishing between the nominal value of the animal and the actual financial burden on the individual. The hadith underscores the flexibility in fiqh regarding sacrificial animals, prioritizing communal benefit over rigid fixed amounts.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina, from Humran who said,

‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The sacricifial animals became too expensive in Mina one year, to the extent that the camel reached one hundred Dinars. So Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> was asked about that, and he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Participate in it’. I said, ‘How many?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Whatever is lighter, so it is superior’. I said, ‘On behalf of how may would it suffice?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘On behalf of seventy’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ‘ibn ‘Udhaynah from Humran who has said the following:

“One year badanah became very expensive in Mina’, so much so that one badanah sold for one hundred dinar. Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about it and he (the Imam) said to share it. I asked, ‘For how many people it is sufficient?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘The lighter the better.’ I asked, ‘For how many?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘For seventy.’”
